notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS; started with Redwood Hosted API (30-day trial) to validate UX flows (contextual help + search). Trial showed functional fit; now moving to Dedicated to meet predictable throughput and data isolation requirements. Customer asked for detailed mapping from Hosted trial telemetry -> Dedicated sizing (QPS -> GPU pool sizing, concurrency estimates, token mix impact on capacity/cost).

Hosted trial highlights (customer-provided telemetry):
- Duration: 2026-01-20 -> 2026-02-19 (30 days).
- Avg QPS (production-like traffic during trial window): 3.8 QPS steady; peak bursts up to 28 QPS during feature releases.
- Avg concurrency: 2.1; peak concurrency observed 18 (10-minute spike during release).
- Token mix: ~72% of requests are short prompts (<=64 prompt tokens) with short completions (~<128 tokens). ~28% are long-context flows (prompt avg 420 tokens, completion avg 450 tokens) used by summarization and long-doc search.
- Token ratio: average total tokens per request ~310 tokens; skewed by heavy summarization workflows.
- Latency: 95th pctl tail at Hosted ~420ms for short requests; long-context generation 95p ~1.8s. Customer target: 95p <=300ms for short UI assist, <=1.2s for long-doc summaries.
- Cost sensitivity: high; looking to reduce per-token cost 25-40% vs Hosted via dedicated quantization/inf optimizations and caching.

Customer asks / requirements for Dedicated sizing:
- Predictable baseline capacity for steady 5 QPS with capacity to handle spikes to 30 QPS for up to 5-10 minutes without failing SLOs.
- Support 25 concurrent decode requests sustained, with headroom to 60 during releases.
- Estimate GPU equivalent sizing and recommended autoscaling policy (min pool, burst pool, scale cooldowns).
- Guidance on model variants: cheapest viable model for fallbacks (lower token quality but preserves latency/cost), and recommended quantization profile.
- Prefix/KV caching recommendations for their long-doc search flows to lower token load.
- Networking/VPC flow diagram for security review and KMS integration notes.

POC / technical notes:
- POC ran with gpt-style open checkpoints (customer used open LLaMA-derivative in trial). They recorded per-request token counts and latencies — we have the sheet (linked).
- SE and Infra ran quick profiling: long generations dominate compute; batching helps but increases latency for interactive short requests. Customer wants hybrid setup: low-latency pool + high-throughput batch pool.
- They are sensitive to cold-start tails; ask for pinning and warm pool suggestions.

Commercial / procurement notes: 
- Interested in 12-month reserved commitment for Dedicated if price point reduces unit cost ~30% over Hosted assumptions.
- Procurement timeline: internal finance + security review in March, exec sign-off April. Forecast close 2026-04.
- Wants line-item for Optimize add-on (automated batching and quantization recommendations).

Quotes from calls: 
- "We need consistency — sometimes the Hosted trial was great, other times UI assist lagged during spikes. We need predictable latency for customers." — Head of Product (call 2026-03-03).
- "If we can get a clear mapping from our trial telemetry to a Dedicated bill and the expected ARR delta, we can sign up for reserved capacity." — CFO (email thread 2026-03-04).

Next steps (owned):
- SE (Riya) to run capacity model based on trial telemetry and provide: recommended GPU pool config, autoscale thresholds, estimated monthly cost for min/avg/peak. Deliver by 2026-03-17.
- AE (Jordan) to schedule budget review with CFO; provide cost/ARR slide.
- Security (Luis/CSM) to circulate VPC network diagram and KMS integration checklist to their infosec by 2026-03-12.
- Follow-up workshop to align on fallback model choices and quantization guardrails (invite ML infra + product).
